summary: Defines the payto URI scheme for designating payment targets. A single scheme for all kinds of payment targets lets applications offer user interactions for payment links and makes it easier to add new payment systems. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Just as a web link points to a page, a payto link points to a place you can send money to. This document defines how to write such a link, whatever payment system is behind it.

subtitle: A unified URI scheme for payment links that works with any payment system.

tldr.problem: Different payment systems (IBAN, Bitcoin, Venmo, etc.) each have their own way to specify where to send money, making it hard for applications to offer a single payment link interface.
tldr.mechanism: The payto URI scheme provides a unified format where the authority identifies the payment type and the path identifies the account, with optional query parameters for amount, payer name, recipient name, and a message.
tldr.outcome: Applications can now handle payment links uniformly, and new payment systems can be registered without changing application code; the scheme has been placed on the IANA URI Schemes registry.

facts.label: Payment target types defined
facts.value: 7 (ach, bic, iban, upi, bitcoin, ilp, void)

today: RFC 8905 is an Informational document that defines the payto URI scheme for designating payment targets. The scheme is registered with IANA as a provisional URI scheme and is maintained by the GNUnet Assigned Numbers Authority (GANA), which operates the Payto Payment Target Types registry.

sections.title: The Payto URI Scheme
sections.content:
The payto URI scheme provides a unified way to designate targets for payments. A payto URI always identifies the destination of a payment, which is typically either a bank account or an open transaction. The authority component of the URI identifies the payment target type (such as iban for IBAN bank transfers, bitcoin for Bitcoin addresses, or upi for India's Unified Payment Interface). The path component identifies the specific account or address within that payment system. Query parameters can specify optional details such as amount, payer name, recipient name, and a payment message.

By providing a single URI scheme for all payment systems, applications can offer consistent user interactions with payment links, and new payment systems can be added to a registry without requiring changes to every application.
sections.eli5: A payto link is like a web link, but instead of pointing to a page, it points to a bank account or payment address. The link says what payment system is being used and what account to pay, and it can also include how much money to send and a message explaining why.

sections.title: How Payto URIs are Structured
sections.content:
A payto URI follows the syntax: payto://authority/path?options. The authority must be an alphabetic string followed by alphanumeric characters, dots, or dashes; it identifies the payment target type and defines how the path should be interpreted. The path component is specific to each payment type and can include multiple segments separated by slashes (for example, an ACH payment includes both a routing number and account number in the path).

When an application handles a payto URI, it MUST first review the payment details with the user and get confirmation before initiating any financial transaction. The application SHOULD also prevent clickjacking attacks. If a payment target type is not recognized, the application MAY still allow the user to view and modify the payment details (the path and options) before proceeding.
sections.eli5: A payto link has the form payto://paymenttype/account?options. The payment type tells you what system is being used (like iban for banks or bitcoin for Bitcoin). The account is the destination's address in that system. The options say how much money and any message to include.

sections.title: Payment Amounts and Standard Fields
sections.content:
All payment target types SHOULD support several standard options (generic options) that describe the payment itself. The amount option specifies how much money to transfer in the format currency:unit.fraction. A 3-letter currency code MUST be an ISO 4217 alphabetic code (such as EUR, USD, or INR). The unit value MUST be less than 2^53, and the fraction (if present) MUST have no more than 8 decimal digits. Commas may be included for readability and MUST be ignored.

The receiver-name option specifies the name of the entity receiving the payment (the creditor). The sender-name option specifies the name of the entity making the payment (the debtor). The message option provides a short message identifying the payment's purpose. The instruction option provides reconciliation instructions to the recipient (for example, an invoice number or reference code). All of these options MAY be subject to lossy conversion, modification, or truncation due to character set limitations in the underlying payment system, except that the instruction field SHOULD NOT be truncated if possible.
sections.eli5: The options in a payto link can say how much money to send (like EUR:100.00), who is paying, who is receiving, and what the money is for (like "Invoice 123").

sections.title: Different Payment System Types
sections.content:
The RFC defines seven payment target types: ach for Automated Clearing House (US bank transfers), bic for Business Identifier Code (for wire transfers between banks), iban for International Bank Account Number (used throughout Europe and many other countries), upi for Unified Payment Interface (India's mobile payment system), bitcoin for Bitcoin addresses, ilp for Interledger Protocol addresses, and void for out-of-band payments like cash.

Each type has different requirements and limitations. For example, IBAN allows an optional BIC component for legacy systems. UPI requires the amount and receiver-name options. Bitcoin uses addresses as defined in BIP 21. The void type allows specifying payment parameters for transactions that happen outside the internet, such as in-person cash payments.

New payment types can be registered in the Payto Payment Target Types registry using a First Come First Served policy.
sections.eli5: The RFC shows how to write payto links for seven different payment systems: bank transfers in the US (ACH) and Europe (IBAN), wire transfers (BIC), India's payment app (UPI), Bitcoin, a newer protocol (ILP), and cash payments.

sections.title: Handling Different Languages and Character Sets
sections.content:
Many payment systems use restricted character sets. Applications that process payto URIs MUST convert characters that are not allowed by the target payment system into allowable characters, either by encoding or replacement. This conversion process MAY be lossy for most options, but the instruction field (which is used for payment reconciliation) SHOULD NOT be truncated if possible.

If converting the instruction field would cause lossy conversion, modification, or truncation, the application SHOULD refuse to proceed with the payment and ask the user to provide a different instruction value.

The payto scheme disallows the userinfo component (username and password) in URIs to avoid special encoding rules. Instead, payment details are passed as query options, where encoding rules are uniform across all options.
sections.eli5: Different payment systems accept different letters and symbols. When an application sends a payto link to a payment system, it may need to change special characters to ones that system accepts. If important information like a reference code would get mangled, the application should ask the user to change it first.
